evidence.ai_role: A tree of trained logistic-regression experts predicts subtype labels from gene expression and transfers mouse taxonomy to human nuclei, enabling the subtype-specific disease comparison.
evidence.tested: Existing mouse/human transcriptomic data; 24,419 mouse reference cells, five-fold cell-stratified validation and a held-out test; human depletion comparison uses eight control and seven Parkinson’s donors with donor-aware mixed models.
evidence.unknown: Causal susceptibility, in-vivo human projections and therapeutic benefit are not established. Cells are not independent donor replicates; cross-species annotation may constrain inferred subtype identity.

organization: Northwestern University; Shirley Ryan AbilityLab; Karolinska Institutet; University of California, San Diego; McGill University

source_review.scope: Primary v1 full-text HMoE training/validation and Human transfer Methods, human population-depletion/MASC Methods, subtype Results and limitations; primary bioRxiv API date independently checked. Numerical drug-target and inferred projection claims not admitted as independent findings.

summary: A hierarchical mixture-of-experts classifier transferred mouse dopaminergic-neuron labels to human single-nucleus datasets, identifying an Anxa1-associated population. The preprint reports this population was more depleted in Parkinson’s disease than comparator subtypes in a postmortem analysis of eight control and seven Parkinson’s donors. The model uses logistic-regression experts trained on a mouse reference; donor-aware abundance models support an association rather than a causal mechanism. Cross-species label transfer, small donor cohorts and retrospective tissue limit generalization; inferred connectivity and candidate drug targets are not direct human tracing or demonstrated therapy.
title: Cross-species classifier identifies a human dopaminergic subtype depleted in Parkinson’s disease
